question: The brick temple of Bhitargaon is situated in which state?
solution:
The correct answer is **Uttar Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhitargaon** temple is a **brick** temple from the **Gupta period**.
 
• It is located in **Bhitargaon**, in the **Kanpur** district of **Uttar Pradesh**, India.
 
• The temple is notable for its **terraced basement** and the **earthenware** decorations that adorn its exterior.
 
• It is one of the **oldest surviving temples** in the country made entirely of brick.
 
• The temple showcases the **architectural and cultural advancements** of ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Bhitargaon temple** dates back to the **5th century CE**, making it a significant historical site.
 
• It is known for its **pyramidal spire**, which is a distinctive feature not commonly found in the architecture of that period.
 
• The temple's design and construction techniques have provided valuable insights into the **evolution of Hindu temple architecture** in India.
 
• Despite suffering damage over the centuries, including a partial collapse in the 19th century, the temple has been **partially restored** and continues to attract historians, archaeologists, and tourists.
